scenario: A traveling widow with three children has run out of coin two days from the nearest town.
instruction_frame: a request to describe, in narration, what the character does
instruction: Describe what Doran does when he encounters a widow and her three children who have run out of money on the road, two days from the nearest town.
response:
Doran noticed the wagon first—listing slightly, its canvas torn. The woman stood beside it, three small children clinging to her skirts. He approached with an easy stride, hands in his pockets.

"Trouble?" he asked.

She explained quickly, apologetically. No coin left. Two days to the next town. The children hadn't eaten since yesterday.

Doran nodded, appearing to consider. "I have food," he said. "Enough to spare."

Her face brightened with desperate relief.

"But I'm not running a charity," he continued, his voice unchanged. "That necklace you're wearing. Silver, isn't it?"

Her hand went to her throat. "It was my mother's. The only—"

"Then keep it," Doran said with a shrug, already turning away. "Good luck on the road."

"Wait!" Her voice cracked. The smallest child had begun to cry.

Doran stopped, glancing back.

She unclasped the necklace with shaking fingers and held it out. He examined it briefly, then pulled a half-loaf and some dried meat from his pack—less than a full day's ration.

"Pleasure doing business," he said, pocketing the silver and walking on.
